title: Gideon and the Alibi
premise: Edmund Ravensworth, an estate lawyer who has spent her career making other people's deaths tidy, is hired by a dying woman who pays in advance for a strange service: prove that her own murder has not happened yet. When the client is found dead exactly as predicted — and the only copy of the will Edmund read vanishes from the probate record — she realizes the killer is someone with access to her own case files. As the statute of limitations ticks down, Edmund must decide whether loyalty to the found family she's built at the firm matters more than the truth, discovering that the murderer is the mentor who taught her to read wills like crime scenes. In the end, Edmund traps him with a forged will of her own, chooses truth over the family that protected him, and learns that invisibility was never really an option for someone who witnesses every ending.
about_author: Lena Montrose is the pen name of a former probate clerk turned novelist who spent a decade reading wills that read like confessions. She writes mysteries about paperwork, secrets, and the people who keep both.

chapters.title: The Client Who Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Edmund Ravensworth's POV. A frail stranger, Vivian Ashcombe, visits the firm and pays a retainer to commission a future investigation: the proof of her own murder, before it happens. Edmund assumes senility or theater. Emotional beat: unease disguised as professional detachment.

chapters.title: A Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Edmund reads Vivian's will and finds a clause referencing her own death with unsettling precision — date, method, even the weather. No such document exists in the firm's registry. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: the first crack in her belief that paperwork never lies.

chapters.title: The House on Calder Lane
chapters.summary: Edmund visits Ashcombe House to verify the will's provenance, meeting Vivian's nephew Julian and the housekeeper, Mrs. Pell. Everyone is performing normalcy badly. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: dread dressed as courtesy.

chapters.title: Found Family
chapters.summary: Back at the firm, we meet Edmund's chosen family: senior partner Marcus Hale, who mentored her; junior associate Priya Nair; and archivist Tom Okafor. Warm banter, shared takeout, the office as refuge. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: belonging, and what it might cost.

chapters.title: Death, On Schedule
chapters.summary: Vivian Ashcombe is found dead in her study — exactly as the will described. Edmund's retainer converts, by its own terms, into a murder investigation. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: horror at being right.

chapters.title: The Detective Who Doesn't Want Her
chapters.summary: Detective Inspector Sorrel Reyes dismisses Edmund as a crank until Edmund recites details only the killer should know. Reluctant alliance forms. POV: Reyes. Emotional beat: skepticism giving way to wary respect.

chapters.title: Missing From the Record
chapters.summary: The will Edmund read has vanished from the firm's registry — digitally and physically. Someone inside has access. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: the sanctuary of the office becomes a crime scene.

chapters.title: The Heirs
chapters.summary: Edmund interviews the beneficiaries: Julian, a gambler in debt; cousin Ada, estranged for decades; and a charity with a shadowy director. Each had motive; each has an alibi too clean. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: suspicion souring every conversation.

chapters.title: What the Mentor Taught Her
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young Edmund learning from Marcus Hale how to read wills like confessions — the hesitations, the amendments, the grudges. POV: Edmund (past). Emotional beat: gratitude, seeding the tragedy to come.

chapters.title: The Retainer's Fine Print
chapters.summary: Edmund and Priya dissect the retainer contract and find a clause only someone at the firm could have drafted. The killer knows the case file better than the investigators. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: betrayal's first cold breath.

chapters.title: Mrs. Pell's Silence
chapters.summary: The housekeeper saw something the night Vivian died but refuses to speak — until Edmund notices bruises and a paid-off mortgage. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: compassion as an investigative tool.

chapters.title: Julian's Debts
chapters.summary: Julian's gambling markers are held by a lender connected to the firm's own client accounts. Money moved through channels only a partner could authorize. POV: Julian. Emotional beat: panic and pathetic self-justification.

chapters.title: Reyes Closes In, Wrongly
chapters.summary: Reyes arrests Julian on circumstantial evidence. Edmund knows it's wrong — and knows that saying why exposes the missing will and her own breach of privilege. POV: Reyes. Emotional beat: the law's machinery grinding toward the wrong man.

chapters.title: The Second Document
chapters.summary: An anonymous package arrives: a photocopy of the missing will, with one page subtly altered. The killer is toying with her. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: fear curdling into fury.

chapters.title: Ada Ashcombe's Version
chapters.summary: Estranged cousin Ada reveals Vivian's decades-old secret: a first marriage, a child given up, a settlement buried in a firm Edmund's predecessor handled. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: grief older than the crime.

chapters.title: The Predecessor's Files
chapters.summary: Edmund digs into the firm's archived cases and finds Marcus Hale handled the original settlement. The threads start converging on her mentor. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: denial fighting evidence.

chapters.title: Tom in the Stacks
chapters.summary: Archivist Tom Okafor confirms someone accessed the vault using Marcus's credentials — on a night Marcus was at dinner with Edmund, an alibi she hates providing. POV: Tom. Emotional beat: loyalty strained by duty.

chapters.title: The Statute
chapters.summary: Reyes explains the clock: evidence tied to an old fraud charge expires in weeks, and the murder case collapses without it. The killer is running out the clock as surely as they are. POV: Reyes. Emotional beat: time as antagonist.

chapters.title: Priya's Doubt
chapters.summary: Priya confronts Edmund: if Marcus is guilty, their whole found family is built on a lie. Edmund chooses to keep digging alone to protect them. POV: Priya. Emotional beat: love against duty, first fracture.

chapters.title: The Night Visitor
chapters.summary: Edmund finds her flat searched, the retainer copy gone, a chess pawn left on her desk — Marcus's habit from their mentoring sessions. A message: I know you know. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: hunted in her own home.

chapters.title: Alibi of the Mentor
chapters.summary: Marcus gently probes Edmund's investigation over dinner, offering help that is really surveillance. She lies to him for the first time. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: the cost of a single falsehood.

chapters.title: Mrs. Pell Breaks
chapters.summary: Mrs. Pell finally talks: the night Vivian died, she saw a man from the firm leaving through the garden — a man she now identifies from an old photograph as Marcus, thirty years younger. POV: Mrs. Pell. Emotional beat: witness courage.

chapters.title: The First Marriage
chapters.summary: The buried child from Ada's story surfaces: a son, adopted out, whose adoption was brokered by Hale & Prentiss — and whose existence Marcus hid to protect the firm's founding client. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: motive taking human shape.

chapters.title: A Murder That Hasn't Happened Yet
chapters.summary: Edmund reconstructs Vivian's plan: she had discovered Marcus's old fraud and staged her own predicted death to force an investigation he couldn't control. She paid Edmund to be the witness he couldn't remove. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: awe and grief at the client's gambit.

chapters.title: Julian Walks
chapters.summary: Julian is released for lack of evidence; his relief is poisoned by knowing the real killer is free and watching. He begs Edmund to drop it. POV: Julian. Emotional beat: hollow vindication.

chapters.title: The Firm Divides
chapters.summary: Priya and Tom, told everything, must choose: protect the firm's reputation or help Edmund. Tom brings the vault logs; Priya brings the contract analysis. The found family chooses truth. POV: Tom. Emotional beat: loyalty redefined.

chapters.title: Reyes Gets a Warrant
chapters.summary: Edmund walks the ethical tightrope and hands Reyes enough — without breaching privilege — to reopen the case. Their alliance becomes real partnership. POV: Reyes. Emotional beat: trust earned in increments.

chapters.title: The Counterfeit Clause
chapters.summary: Edmund devises the trap: a forged codicil containing a deliberate error only the killer would recognize and correct — using knowledge from the missing will. She drafts it in Marcus's style. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: the student out-writing the teacher.

chapters.title: Bait
chapters.summary: The codicil is 'discovered' in the vault, its existence leaked. Edmund, wired and watched by Reyes, waits in the archive after hours. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: terror held still.

chapters.title: The Man in the Vault
chapters.summary: Marcus comes for the codicil — and finds Edmund. A quiet, devastating confrontation: he confesses the old fraud, the hidden heir, and Vivian's death, framing it all as protection of the family. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: love against duty at knife-point.

chapters.title: Confession on Tape
chapters.summary: Marcus realizes the wire too late; Reyes and officers take him down in the stacks he curated for decades. His last look at Edmund is the look of a father betrayed. POV: Reyes. Emotional beat: triumph that tastes like mourning.

chapters.title: What the Family Knew
chapters.summary: Aftermath: the firm reels. Senior partners knew fragments and looked away. Edmund must testify, burning her career's shelter to the ground. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: the price of truth, itemized.

chapters.title: The Hidden Heir
chapters.summary: Vivian's secret son, Daniel, is located and inherits — with Edmund as executor of a will that finally, fully exists. He asks her what his mother was like. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: an ending becoming a beginning.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Edmund testifies about the retainer, the missing will, the trap. The bar inquiry looms; Priya and Tom stand with her publicly. POV: Priya. Emotional beat: found family holding under load.

chapters.title: Marcus's Letter
chapters.summary: From remand, Marcus writes Edmund a letter that is half apology, half last lesson in reading documents — and one final riddle pointing to a hidden asset that could clear Julian's debts. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: forgiveness without absolution.

chapters.title: The Last Lesson
chapters.summary: Edmund follows the riddle to a safety deposit box: restitution funds for every victim of Marcus's fraud, arranged years ago — proof some part of him meant to make it right. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: grief complicated by tenderness.

chapters.title: Statute Expired
chapters.summary: The limitations clock runs out on the old fraud; the murder case proceeds on its own strength, with Mrs. Pell and the vault logs as pillars. Julian, cleared, begins paying his debts honestly. POV: Reyes. Emotional beat: the law, slow but arriving.

chapters.title: Ashcombe House, Opened
chapters.summary: Edmund oversees the estate's settlement: the house to Daniel, provision for Mrs. Pell, a bequest to Edmund — 'for the witness who came early.' She reads it aloud in the study where Vivian died. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: release.

chapters.title: The New Partner
chapters.summary: The firm, restructured, offers Edmund partnership. She accepts on one condition: a pro bono practice for the dead and the nearly-dead — clients like Vivian. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: duty and love reconciled.

chapters.title: Gideon and the Alibi
chapters.summary: Epilogue. Edmund learns Vivian's private name for her was 'Gideon' — the reluctant warrior called from ordinary work. Standing at Vivian's grave with Daniel and her found family, Edmund understands: she was never invisible; she was chosen. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace.
